After the fix, the same command -> 2 passed. Full tests/test_dashboard_app.py: 143 passed twice, once before the commit and once after. An intermediate fix attempt that used call_after_refresh(self.paint) gave 142 passed, 1 failed: test_q_quits hit NoMatches because the deferred paint ran during teardown. I dropped that approach. test_q_quits passed 5/5 when run alone.
observations: I added temporary prints to the unfixed code and ran the resize test. On resize to 60, DashboardApp.on_resize received Resize(size=60x40), but self.size and self.screen.size still read 120. paint() therefore called EffortPane.show(width=120). Next, EffortPane.on_resize saw scrollable_content_region.width=58 != inner=118. It re-called show(*self.last), which replayed the stored width 120. The table kept the 5-column set (status, task, wave, phase, assignee) until the next reload.
root_cause: DashboardApp.on_resize runs before Textual updates App.size, so paint() reads the old width from self.size.width. EffortPane.on_resize then replays the stale width stored in self.last. Neither path ever passes the new width to task_columns(). Fix: on_resize passes event.size.width to paint(width), and paint uses it for the header and the panes. EffortPane.on_resize re-shows with self.app.size.width, not the stored width. The diff touches only paint, both on_resize handlers and the events import. It adds one new test and no shared test helpers change.
